svg.aria-label: Four gameplay charts: switch-access reach time against target count, hover budget against gap width, the gravity zone reader matrix, and the touch scheme fingerprint.
svg.title: Four charts this project needed
svg.desc: Each chart turns an adjective into a shape. Two produce a number we did not previously have: the scan group size, and the hover budget The Split actually requires.

g.inkscape:label: 10 Title
g.text: Each one turns an adjective into a shape. Two of them produce a number nobody had picked.

g.inkscape:label: 20 Scan reach time
g.text: 1 · FLAT SCANNING IS UNUSABLE PAST ABOUT 15 TARGETS
Worst-case seconds to reach one operation by switch scanning, at the default 1.5 s per element.
THE NUMBER: best group size is the square root of the target count. For the editor's forty, groups of SIX.

g.inkscape:label: 30 Hover budget
g.text: 2 · THE SPLIT NEEDS 0.36 s OF HOVER, NOT MORE
Hover seconds required to clear a gap, given a 3.4 m jump. Two approach speeds from the move set.

g.inkscape:label: feasible band
g.text: ceiling: 0.8 s before a 1.5 m/s clamp drops you past the ledge
THE NUMBER: a 0.8 s budget and a 1.5 m/s clamp clears every gap up to 9 m. That is the whole feature.

g.inkscape:label: 40 Gravity matrix
g.text: Who reads a GravityZoneComponent, and what happens when they do.
The default row crossed with the common controller is the one dead cell. That is the whole bug.
It took a session to find in code and is a glance here. The fastest bug report is often a four cell matrix.

g.inkscape:label: 50 Touch fingerprint
g.text: 4 · WHY A BUTTON APPEARS WHEN YOU DROP IN A COMPONENT
The touch scheme is rebuilt from a fingerprint, not authored. Three inputs, one rebuild, two outputs.
both outputs come from the same preset, which is why a scene never shows a control it does not have
This is not a bug, and it surprises people, so it is a WATCH OUT rather than a gap.
Nothing was authored. Drop a component in, the fingerprint changes, the scheme rebuilds, a button exists.

g.inkscape:label: 99 Footer
g.text: Charts 1 and 2 are DERIVED from values read out of the engine, so they are arithmetic rather than opinion. Charts 3 and 4 are structural and describe what the code does today.
None of the four is a measurement of a running build. Nothing here has been profiled.
